messages:
Maya R: Heads up — we onboarded Asterion-v1q (PTQ int8) into the canary pool this morning. Throughput looks promising but we're seeing a spike in structured-output/toolcall parse failures. canary-bot posted the run: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/asterion-v1q

Ravi P: How bad is the spike compared to the fp16 baseline? :thinking:

Lucy (ML Infra): Short summary from telemetry: toolcall JSON parse failures = 3.72% on current canary (n=1200). Baseline FP16 is ~0.18%. The majority are either missing closing brace, trailing comma, or free-text appended after the JSON object.

Dave: Example from a failing sample (copied from canary artifacts):
```
{"action": "search", "args": {"q": "redwood inference"},
  "meta": {"confidence": 0.82}
}
Follow-up: Found more results on the docs page...
```
Notice the JSON itself has an extra newline/closing brace but then there is extra sentence appended — breaks our parser.

Maya R: Reproduced locally with int8 binary + kv-cache enabled, batch_size=8. When kv-cache is on we see higher suffix noise. Hypothesis: quantization + streaming/chunking boundary produces subtle tokenization/punctuation shifts that lead to trailing free-text after the expected object.

Ravi P: Two quick mitigations: 1) enable a post-processing rescue (json_wrap / greedy-last-brace) in the serving path as a short-term patch; 2) run bisect across quant config (per-tensor vs per-channel calibration, clip range) and canary again with kv-cache disabled. I'll take the bisect.

Lucy (ML Infra): I've exported the top 200 failing prompts to the eval harness (eval-run: erun-175800A). We should run the exact same prompts against fp16, int8(per-tensor), int8(per-channel), and int8 with kv-cache off. Also add a streaming boundary test that slices responses into 32-token chunks — we saw boundary fragments in earlier PTQ runs.

canary-bot: Canary summary: model=Asterion-v1q(int8), samples=1200, toolcall_parse_fail=3.72%, mean_latency=142ms, link=https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/asterion-v1q/results

Dave: Small note — some failures are "well-formed JSON" but with swapped field order or extra fields; our strict schema linter rejects them. For short-term acceptance, do we want schema-soften on canary only?

Maya R: I'd rather not soften the schema for canary — we need signal. Short-term plan: add a non-blocking rescue step that attempts to repair common suffix issues (strip trailing sentences, find last balanced brace, run json.loads heuristic). If rescue succeeds, mark as rescued in telemetry. If not, fail as before. That gives us visibility while reducing user-facing breakage.

Ravi P: Action items: @Ravi -> run quant-bisect (per-tensor vs per-channel) + repeat canary w/kv-cache off by EOD. @Lucy -> push failing prompts into a regression test and run evaluations across the variants. @Dave -> prototype the non-blocking json_rescue in the serving adapter.

Lucy (ML Infra): I'll also add a histogram of failure modes (trailing-text, missing-brace, trailing-comma, extra-fields) so we can prioritize fixes.

Maya R: Agreed. Hold rollout until either parse_fail < 0.5% or we have a patch + accepted rescue telemetry. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
